statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, say *at worst nodal of relative dimension one* if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and each nonempty geometric fibre is an equidimensional one-dimensional scheme with at-worst-nodal singularities. Equivalently $f$ is syntomic of relative dimension one and $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, defined by the first Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/S}$, is unramified over $S$. Here syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres. This property is stable under base change and local for the étale topology on the source and fpqc topology on the target.

A smooth morphism of relative dimension $1$ is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locus-where-nodal}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is flat and
locally of finite presentation. Then there is a maximal open
subscheme $U \subset X$ such that $f|_U : U \to S$ is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$. Moreover, formation
of $U$ commutes with arbitrary base change.

\item $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation,
\end{enumerate}
then there exists an $i \geq 0$ such that $f_i$ is at-worst-nodal
of relative dimension $1$.

\item $f$ is proper,
\item $f$ is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension $1$, and
\item the geometric fibres of $f$ are connected.
\end{enumerate}
Then (a) $f_*\mathcal{O}_X = \mathcal{O}_S$ and this holds after
any base change, (b) $R^1f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a finite locally free
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module whose formation commutes with any base change,
and (c) $R^qf_*\mathcal{O}_X = 0$ for $q \geq 2$.
hypotheses: Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, say *at worst nodal of relative dimension one* if $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and each nonempty geometric fibre is an equidimensional one-dimensional scheme with at-worst-nodal singularities. Equivalently $f$ is syntomic of relative dimension one and $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, defined by the first Fitting ideal of $\Omega_{X/S}$, is unramified over $S$. Here syntomic means flat, locally of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres. This property is stable under base change and local for the étale topology on the source and fpqc topology on the target.
